The incidence rate of atrial fibrillation ([[atrieflimren]]) in [[Danmark]] is a key epidemiological metric tracked by the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]]. Monitoring these rates across all Danish regions—[[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]]—provides critical insights into the national burden of the disease and the subsequent risk of severe complications.

According to the 2023 annual report, the incidence rate of atrial fibrillation in Denmark was 3.3 per 1,000 inhabitants during the reporting period [^src1]. More recent data from the 2024 report indicates that the incidence rate increased slightly to 3.7 per 1,000 inhabitants in 2023/2024 [^src3]. 

Beyond the initial diagnosis, tracking the incidence rate of secondary complications is vital for understanding patient outcomes. Nationally, 0.8% of the incident atrial fibrillation population develops an intracranial hemorrhage ([[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]]) within one year of their diagnosis [^src2]. Furthermore, the incidence of heart failure ([[hjertesvigtsindikatoren]]) among newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients is also significant; for the period between July 1, 2021, and June 30, 2022, 6.5% (95% CI: 6.1–6.8) of these patients developed heart failure within one year [^src4].
